fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The elders were summoned, but they didn't go up alone. Josiah, king of Judah, went up to the house of the LORD with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests and the prophets too. The text says “…all the people small and great…” That's a whole crowd, and not a committee.

Copying is a fine thing to do with a book, but that's not what the text says here. It says that in their hearing he read all the words of the Book of the Covenant. The people heard every word of it, straight from the king.

Doorkeepers are in the verse, so I see the mix-up. But the order isn't about money. Josiah commanded Hilkiah, the priests second in rank and the doorkeepers to remove the articles made for Baal, Asherah and all the host of heaven from the temple of the LORD. Those were idol things, not cash.

That's the word. Josiah brought all the priests from the cities of Judah and desecrated the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where the priests had burned incense. That's a long stretch of ground, from one end to the other. Josiah's reach was wide.

That's what the text says. Josiah desecrated Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom “…so that no one could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the chapter. The text shows Josiah closing that place down.

Guarding means keeping something safe, and that's not what happens here. The text shows Josiah pulling down those altars and pulverizing them. After that, he threw their dust into the Kidron Valley. Those altars were not being protected, friend.

The text doesn't say he left it. At Bethel, Josiah pulled down the altar and burned the high place. He ground it to powder and then burned the Asherah pole (2 Kings 23:15). The pole went into the fire.
That's right. At Bethel, Josiah pulled down the altar, burned the high place and ground it to powder. Then verse 15 says he “…burned the Asherah pole.” The pole did not stay standing.

Jeroboam, the king of Israel, is in the chapter, but not at this tomb. Verse 15 says he set up the high place at Bethel and caused Israel to sin. The men of the city said this tomb belongs to the man of God who came from Judah. That's a different man entirely.

I understand the mix-up, since Josiah did have bones burned on the altar at Bethel. But when he heard whose tomb it was, he said, “Let him rest…” He also said, “Do not let anyone disturb his bones.” So that tomb stayed as it was.
